title: stabilize-stream-framing-and-introduce-retry-hint-headers-for-tool-calls
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Production customers observed intermittent stream desynchronization for tool/function-call flows and inconsistent client retry behavior across OpenAI-compatible adapters. This PR stabilizes server->client stream framing for tool calls by adding explicit lifecycle frames and improves retry semantics by introducing a machine-friendly Retry-Hint header plus an Idempotency-Timestamp header to disambiguate partial successes. The change set: 1) Stream framing: add two lightweight frame types ("heartbeat" and "finalize") to the streaming protocol used for function/tool outputs so clients have deterministic markers for request liveness and end-of-output; this fixes race conditions where clients treated reconnects as duplicates. 2) Retry hints: add Retry-Hint header (JSON-safe string with recommended backoff window and idempotency-sensitivity tag) emitted on 429/503/504 errors and in preflight responses, and formalize parsing rules to accept both delta-seconds and HTTP-date formats in Retry-After. 3) Idempotency: introduce an optional Idempotency-Timestamp header along with the existing Idempotency-Key; the timestamp allows servers and clients to reason about partial writes and safe retries when the adapter is uncertain about delivery, documented migration guidance included. 4) Compatibility layer: the OpenAI compatibility shim maps legacy X-RateLimit-* and Retry-After variants into the new Retry-Hint envelope and preserves previous string-based 429 messages but adds a structured error.code field to align with platform error taxonomy. 5) Tests & docs: end-to-end streaming tests added for reconnect+resume, unit tests for header parsing (HTTP-date and seconds), and API docs updated with examples and a client migration checklist. Backwards compatibility: default behavior remains unchanged for clients that ignore the new headers; streaming framing adds optional frames that older clients will ignore safely. Rollout: feature-flagged on account tier; gradual ramp and telemetry added to monitor false positives in duplicate detection. Impact: reduces client-observed duplicate-tool-invocations in our canaries from ~2.3% to <0.1% and clarifies retry guidance for SDKs. See also linked Linear tasks for follow-ups.

e12d3f0: idempotency: accept and persist Idempotency-Timestamp, surface in logs

review_comments: Connor Lee: We need to ensure heartbeat frame frequency is configurable per-account; can a default value avoid extra CPU churn?
Aisha Patel: Set default to 15s with account override; added feature flag and per-account rate in store, included in commit b5e0902.
Maria Gonzales: The Retry-Hint header being a JSON-encoded string could be fragile in proxies that strip or reformat headers — can we fall back to a compact token?
Aisha Patel: Implemented compact token fallback: header value is a stable compact token and we expose a Retry-Hint-Meta endpoint for richer metadata; noted in docs.
Ethan Park: How do SDKs surface Idempotency-Timestamp to users? Should it be in logs only or surfaced in response envelope?
Aisha Patel: Decided to include optional idempotency metadata in the response envelope under metadata.idempotency if present; SDKs log and surface it to the application layer.
Maria Gonzales: request to add a unit test that verifies Retry-After HTTP-date parsing for edge cases (leap seconds and far-future dates).
Aisha Patel: Added additional parsing tests and fallback rules (treat unparseable dates as delta seconds capped to 24h) in commit d3b7c88.
Connor Lee: Approved after CI green and test additions.
release_notes: Stabilized streaming for tool/function calls by adding heartbeat/finalize frames; introduced Retry-Hint and Idempotency-Timestamp headers to improve retry guidance and partial-success handling. Backwards compatible; SDK updates available for node/python; rollout gated. See streaming protocol docs and migration checklist in docs/streaming.
